summary: Paul Horsch worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Paris (1947), taught French at Visva-Bharati University (1952–1956), and was apl. Professor of Indology at the University of Zurich (1967–1971).

Paul J. Griffiths specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Oxford and Wisconsin-Madison, later holding professorships at the University of Chicago, University of Illinois Chicago (2000–2007), and Duke University (ca. 2008–2017).
Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2002). He held program manager posts at USC (2020–2022) and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (2022).
Paul Kiparsky is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Morris Halle at MIT (ca. 1962–1965). He joined Stanford University around 1984.

Paul Kretschmer was a linguist who earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1884–1889) under Johannes Schmidt and Hermann Diels. He was a professor at Marburg (1897–1899) and the University of Vienna (1899–1936).

Paul L. Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota (attested 1985). He served as professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).
Paul Marriot Wynch was an Indology scholar who joined the Bengal Civil Service in 1808 and studied at East India Company College from 1809 to 1810.

Paul Masson-Oursel worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under scholars including Alfred Foucher, Sylvain Lévi, and Émile Durkheim. He spent his career at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, serving as Directeur d’études from 1927 to 1953.

Paul McBain specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Chicago (2013–2015), earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (2018–2021), and became a lecturer at Thammasat University in 2021.

Paul Mendes-Flohr worked in religious studies and philosophy, earning his doctorate from Brandeis University. He served as director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and was a professor of Modern Jewish History and Thought at the University of Chicago (ca. 1999–2024).
Paul Michael Toomey specialized in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia (ca. 1974–1984) and taught at Cornell University from ca. 1988 to 1992.

Paul Mus worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology, earning a doctorate from the University of Paris. He held major posts at EFEO (1927–1940), EPHE (1937), Yale (1950), and the Collège de France (1946–1969).

Paul Olaf Bodding was a linguist and Indologist who earned his theological degree at the University of Oslo (1883–1889). He served as head of The Santal Mission of the Northern Churches from 1910 to 1933.

Paul Oltramare worked in Indology and religious studies, studying under Michel Bréal and Paul Deussen. He taught at Collège Calvin (1876–1895) and served as Professor of History of Religions at the University of Geneva (1893–1927).
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (ca. 1881–1889). He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ca. 1887 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot worked in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO (1900) and was a professor at the Collège de France from 1909 to 1945.

Paul R. Brass was a scholar of Indology who studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He spent his career at the University of Washington from ca. 1967 to 2008, where he became Professor Emeritus.

Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Abel Bergaigne and completed his PhD at the University of Paris. He occupied the Sanskrit chair at the University of Lyon from 1887 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur was a philosopher who studied at Rennes and Paris. He held professorships at the University of Strasbourg (1948–1956), Faculty of Arts of Paris (ca. 1956–1965), Paris Nanterre (1964–1970), and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).
